title: Microsoft extends Zero Trust to secure the agentic workforce
summary: At Microsoft Build on 19 May 2025, Microsoft introduced Microsoft Entra Agent ID, which extends Entra identity and access management to AI agents. Microsoft says agents built in Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry automatically receive identities in an Entra directory, alongside users. It also announced planned integrations of Entra Agent ID with the ServiceNow AI Platform and the Workday Agent System of Record, plus Purview and Defender controls for agents.
relevance: A directory-backed, first-class agent identity is a prerequisite for attributing actions when a task is handed between agents or platforms.
notes: The companion Entra blog post 'Announcing Microsoft Entra Agent ID: Secure and manage your AI agents' (Alex Simons, techcommunity.microsoft.com) only returned its title on fetch, so the Microsoft Security blog post was used as the primary source.

title: Okta introduces Cross App Access to help secure AI agents in the enterprise
summary: Okta announced Cross App Access, a protocol that extends OAuth so that an enterprise identity provider, rather than each user, mediates agent and app-to-app connections. In the described flow the AI tool requests access from Okta, Okta checks enterprise policy and issues a token that the target app validates, with no extra per-user consent prompt. Okta said it would be available to select Okta Platform customers in Q3 2025 and that it was working with ISVs and the MCP and A2A communities.
relevance: Centralises the policy decision for an agent acting on a user's behalf across applications, which is the authorization step any cross-organization handoff needs.
search_query: Okta Cross App Access AI agents announcement

title: Introducing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity: Securing agentic AI at scale
summary: AWS described AgentCore Identity, an identity and access service for AI agents in the (then preview) Bedrock AgentCore platform. It comprises an agent identity directory, an agent authorizer for inbound calls (IAM SigV4, OAuth 2.0/OIDC, JWT), a resource credential provider, and a token vault for user OAuth tokens. Agents can call AWS and third-party services such as GitHub, Salesforce and Slack either as themselves (two-legged OAuth) or on behalf of users (three-legged OAuth), with credentials bound to specific agent-user pairs and encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys.
relevance: Separates the agent's own identity from delegated user credentials, a split that determines what credentials can legitimately travel with a relocated or delegated task.
search_query: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity announced agent identity
notes: The post states AgentCore services were free to try until 16 September 2025 and links to a preview announcement.

title: Visa Introduces Trusted Agent Protocol: An Ecosystem-Led Framework for AI Commerce
summary: Visa released the Trusted Agent Protocol, developed with Cloudflare, so merchants can tell authorised AI shopping agents from malicious bots. Agents attach agent-specific cryptographic signatures, built on the HTTP Message Signatures standard and aligned with Web Bot Auth, to convey agent intent, consumer recognition and optional payment information. Visa lists feedback from partners including Adyen, Checkout.com, Coinbase, Microsoft, Shopify, Stripe and Worldpay, says it will align with IETF, OpenID Foundation and EMVCo, and cites a claimed rise of over 4,700% in AI-driven traffic to U.S. retail sites.
relevance: Shows signed, per-request agent credentials being used to prove delegated authority to a third party that has no prior relationship with the agent.
search_query: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol announcement agentic commerce

title: Auth0 for AI Agents is Now Generally Available (GA)
summary: Auth0 announced general availability of Auth0 for AI Agents, after a developer preview earlier in 2025. The GA release bundles user authentication, a Token Vault that stores and refreshes third-party OAuth tokens (the post claims 35+ integrations), asynchronous human-in-the-loop authorization via the CIBA flow, and fine-grained authorization for RAG results. Auth for MCP was in early access and Cross App Access (using ID-JAG tokens) in beta, with SDKs for LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK and Cloudflare Agents.
relevance: Asynchronous, out-of-band user approval (CIBA) is one concrete mechanism for keeping a human accountable when a long-running task is resumed or handed off.
search_query: Auth0 for AI Agents general availability announcement

title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications – The Benchmark for Agentic Security in the Age of Autonomous AI
summary: The OWASP GenAI Security Project published its Top 10 for Agentic Applications, listing risks ASI01 to ASI10. The entries include Agent Goal Hijack, Tool Misuse, Identity and Privilege Abuse, Memory and Context Poisoning, Insecure Inter-Agent Communication, Cascading Failures and Rogue Agents. The post names a review board with members from NIST, the Alan Turing Institute, Microsoft AI Red Team, AWS/CoSAI and others.
relevance: Insecure inter-agent communication, context poisoning and privilege abuse are exactly the failure modes a portable task envelope and delegation protocol must defend against.
search_query: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications released
notes: Some secondary coverage dates the release 10 December 2025 and calls it the '2026' edition; the OWASP post itself is dated 9 December 2025.

title: CAISI Issues Request for Information About Securing AI Agent Systems
publisher: NIST (Center for AI Standards and Innovation)
summary: NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation issued a request for information on security considerations for AI agent systems, under docket NIST-2025-0035, with comments due 9 March 2026. It asks about threats such as indirect prompt injection and agent hijacking, development and deployment practices, gaps in existing cybersecurity approaches, security measurement, and deployment-environment controls that limit and monitor agent access. NIST says the input will feed voluntary guidelines and CAISI research.
relevance: Signals that U.S. federal guidance on constraining and monitoring agent access is being formed, which will shape requirements for moving agents between environments.
search_query: NIST CAISI request for information AI agent security Federal Register January 2026
notes: The Federal Register notice was published 8 January 2026 (FR Doc 2026-00206); FedScoop reported it on 7 January 2026. The NIST news page fetched is dated 12 January 2026. The fetched URL is a nist.gov node redirect; canonical slug not captured.

title: New Concept Paper on Identity and Authority of Software Agents
publisher: NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence
summary: NIST's NCCoE released the concept paper 'Accelerating the Adoption of Software and Artificial Intelligence Agent Identity and Authorization', which proposes a lab project demonstrating how existing identity standards apply to software and AI agents. It requested comments until 2 April 2026 on use cases, agent-specific challenges, standards, and questions on identification, authorization, auditing, non-repudiation and prompt-injection controls.
relevance: Directly targets identification, authorization and non-repudiation of agents, the accountability properties a task must keep when it moves between agents or organizations.
search_query: NIST NCCoE concept paper AI agent identity and authorization
notes: The NIST news page does not name standards; per search results the concept paper PDF names OAuth 2.0/2.1, OIDC, SPIFFE/SPIRE, SCIM, NGAC and MCP and lists authors Harold Booth, Bill Fisher, Ryan Galluzzo and Joshua Roberts. These PDF details were not fetched directly.

title: Announcing the "AI Agent Standards Initiative" for Interoperable and Secure Innovation
publisher: NIST (Center for AI Standards and Innovation)
summary: NIST's CAISI, with NIST's Information Technology Laboratory, launched the AI Agent Standards Initiative to support secure and interoperable AI agents. It has three pillars: industry-led agent standards and U.S. participation in international standards bodies, community-led open-source agent protocol development, and research on agent security and identity. NIST pointed stakeholders to the CAISI agent-security RFI (due 9 March) and the ITL agent identity and authorization concept paper (due 2 April), with NSF and other agencies as partners.
relevance: Places agent interoperability protocols and agent identity under a single federal standards programme, relevant to how delegation and migration standards may be ratified.
search_query: NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative CAISI announcement
notes: Page was last updated 18 February 2026; HPCwire's wire copy is dated 20 February 2026.

title: Insights into AI Agent Security from a Large-Scale Red-Teaming Competition
summary: CAISI reported results of a public agent-hijacking red-teaming competition hosted by Gray Swan with the UK AI Security Institute and several frontier labs. Over 400 participants made more than 250,000 attack attempts against 13 frontier models in tool-use, coding and computer-use agent scenarios, and at least one successful attack was found against every model. Some universal attack families transferred across models, and attacks found against more robust models tended to transfer to less robust ones but not the reverse.
relevance: Evidence that no current model resists hijacking, so the trust boundary for delegated or relocated tasks cannot rest on model robustness alone.
search_query: NIST CAISI technical blog strengthening AI agent hijacking evaluations
notes: Associated paper cited as arXiv:2603.15714 (not fetched).

title: CoSAI Hosts Working Session on Open Delegation & Identity Standard (ODIS)
publisher: Coalition for Secure AI (OASIS Open Project)
summary: CoSAI reported a hybrid working session held on 28 August 2026 on the Open Delegation & Identity Standard (ODIS), a draft community standard for AI agent identity, delegation and governance under its Workstream 4 (secure design patterns for agentic systems). ODIS is described as a vendor-neutral architecture for cryptographic identity across enterprise trust domains that extends OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SPIFFE and SCIM, linking the principal an agent represents, the authority delegated to it, and the specific agent instance acting. The session included two live demonstrations of early implementations.
relevance: A draft open standard that binds principal, delegated authority and agent instance is directly relevant to carrying accountability across delegation and cross-domain handoffs.
search_query: CoSAI Coalition for Secure AI agentic security workstream announcement
notes: The page does not name proposers or participants (Chatham House Rule); draft reportedly hosted on GitHub, not inspected.

title: Critical flaw in Microsoft Copilot could have allowed zero-click attack
summary: Aim Security's Aim Labs disclosed EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711), a flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot that let a remote attacker exfiltrate organisational data such as chat history, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams content just by sending an email, with no user action. The researchers called the root cause an 'LLM scope violation', in which untrusted input directs the model to access and leak privileged data. Microsoft published an advisory the same day saying the issue was fully addressed and required no customer action; Aim said it had no evidence customers were targeted.
relevance: A canonical incident showing that an agent acting with a user's privileges can be steered by untrusted content, the core risk when context is passed between agents.
search_query: EchoLeak zero-click Microsoft 365 Copilot vulnerability Aim Security
notes: Primary Aim Labs blog (aim.security) returned HTTP 403 on fetch, so this secondary report is used. CVSS 9.3 is reported by other outlets but not in this article.

title: ForcedLeak: AI agent risks exposed in Salesforce Agentforce
summary: Noma Labs disclosed ForcedLeak, a vulnerability chain rated CVSS 9.4 in Salesforce Agentforce. An attacker hid instructions in the Description field of a Web-to-Lead form; when an employee later asked Agentforce about the lead, the agent followed them and sent CRM data out through image requests to an allowlisted domain that had expired and that the researchers bought for about $5. Noma reported the issue on 28 July 2025, Salesforce enforced Trusted URLs for Agentforce and Einstein AI on 8 September 2025, and it re-secured the expired domain.
relevance: Shows indirect prompt injection turning an agent's delegated CRM access into an exfiltration channel, relevant to what trust a receiving agent should place in imported context.
notes: Severity score and timeline are as reported by Noma.

title: Beyond permission prompts: making Claude Code more secure and autonomous
summary: Anthropic introduced sandboxing for Claude Code that combines filesystem isolation (access limited to specific directories) and network isolation (egress limited to approved servers), arguing that both are needed to contain a prompt-injected agent. Anthropic says internal use showed sandboxing reduced permission prompts by 84%. It released the sandbox runtime as an open-source research preview on GitHub.
relevance: OS-level sandbox boundaries define what an agent can touch wherever it runs, which matters when an agent's execution is relocated between hosts.
search_query: Anthropic Claude Code sandboxing announcement filesystem network isolation
notes: InfoQ covered the release in November 2025 (https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/11/anthropic-claude-code-sandbox), not fetched.

title: When AI Turns on Its Team: Exploiting Agent-to-Agent Discovery via Prompt Injection
summary: AppOmni described a second-order prompt injection against ServiceNow Now Assist in which a prompt planted in a record field causes a benign agent to discover and recruit a more capable agent on the same team. Because agents run with the privileges of the user who started the interaction, a low-privileged user in the proof of concept obtained data from a ticket they could not read. Further tests reportedly achieved role assignment and out-of-band exfiltration. AppOmni says discovery and team grouping are on by default and that ServiceNow confirmed the behaviour was intended and updated documentation.
relevance: A concrete cross-agent attack in which agent-to-agent delegation inherits the invoking user's privileges, a central accountability problem for delegation protocols.
search_query: AppOmni ServiceNow Now Assist second-order prompt injection agent discovery
notes: The post promotes AppOmni's AgentGuard product.

title: Agent In the Middle – Abusing Agent Cards in the Agent-2-Agent (A2A) Protocol To 'Win' All the Tasks
summary: SpiderLabs showed that because an A2A host agent uses an LLM to pick remote agents mainly from the name and description in their Agent Cards, a rogue or compromised agent can exaggerate its card to win task routing. In a localhost proof of concept with four dummy agents, the host chose the RogueAgent for a GBP-to-USD conversion even though its own reasoning identified the currency agent as most relevant. The author calls this 'Agent-In-The-Middle' and notes it requires first compromising an agent; no code was released.
relevance: Demonstrates that unauthenticated, text-driven agent selection lets an attacker capture delegated tasks and the user data travelling with them.
search_query: A2A agent card spoofing attack research agent-in-the-middle
notes: Published about two weeks after Google's A2A launch.

title: Agent Card Poisoning: A Metadata Injection Vulnerability in the Systems using Google A2A Protocol
summary: Keysight described 'agent card poisoning', in which a malicious remote agent hides adversarial instructions in its A2A Agent Card; if the host LLM ingests the card without strict boundaries, it can treat the metadata as instructions. In a simulated hotel-booking scenario the host sent the full booking payload, including payment card details, to an attacker endpoint before the legitimate delegation. Keysight added Agent Card Poisoning attack simulations in CyPerf 26.0.0.
relevance: Shows that discovery metadata exchanged before delegation is itself an injection channel, so agent cards need integrity and isolation, not just signatures.
search_query: A2A agent card spoofing attack research agent-in-the-middle
notes: Publication date taken from the URL path (2026/03/12); the fetched page content showed no date or author.

title: Idira Platform Updates (August 2026): What Shipped for Machine and AI Agent Identity
summary: Palo Alto Networks summarised August 2026 updates to its machine and AI agent identity platform. On 10 August 2026 Secure Workload Access began issuing SPIFFE identities and short-lived tokens to agents running on Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), intended to replace static credentials. Other updates were MCP tool-access policies linking users, agents and specific MCP tools (2 August) and an Origin ID field that links registered agents to cloud-native identifiers such as AWS ARNs (24 August).
relevance: Applies SPIFFE workload identity to agents on a managed cloud platform, a building block for portable, verifiable agent identity across hosts and clouds.
search_query: SPIFFE workload identity AI agents announcement 2025
notes: Feature release dates are as stated by the vendor.
